text:
jordan-support: Heads-up — customer reported invoice INV-2026-089 charged UK VAT (20%) even though billing address + VAT ID are German. They want a corrected invoice and explanation. They noticed the VAT line specifically shows country GB.

liz-billing: Can you paste the invoice number, the billed-to country and the VAT ID they provided? Also any payment method country we can see?

jordan-support: Invoice INV-2026-089, billed-to country: DE, VAT ID: DE123456789, billing address: Berlin, Germany. Payment method brand: VISA, card country in payment instrument metadata: GB. Customer says they selected Germany at checkout.

mark-finance: If card BIN country is GB and our tax lookup used payment instrument country before validating VAT ID, that could explain it. For EU B2B with a valid VAT ID we typically apply reverse charge (no VAT). Did our VAT validation call return success?

tax-bot: tax-service log snippet (sanitized):
```
2026-03-05T09:12:21Z INFO tax.lookup request_id=abc-789 payload={"billing_country":"DE","vat_id":"DE123456789","payment_country":"GB"}
2026-03-05T09:12:21Z INFO tax.resolve jurisdiction=GB reason="payment_instrument_country_took_priority"
2026-03-05T09:12:21Z INFO tax.compute tax_rate=0.20 tax_label="UK VAT"
```

ops-sre: Repro steps for local dev:
1) Create test customer with billing_country=DE and vat_id=DE123456789
2) Attach payment method with metadata {"country":"GB"} (use test card from gateway)
3) Trigger invoice creation via /v1/invoices endpoint with line items for subscription
4) Observe tax-service decision in logs (see above)

liz-billing: Thanks. For remediation we should: 1) Issue a full credit note for INV-2026-089 reversing the charged VAT, 2) Reissue a corrected invoice either 0% (reverse charge) showing the validated DE VAT ID OR apply DE VAT at 19% if the sale is taxable and customer is non-business — but they gave a VAT ID so reverse charge applies.

mark-finance: Agreed. Also we need to correct the root cause: tax-service should prefer validated VAT ID / billing_country for jurisdiction for B2B EU sales, not payment instrument country. Change request queued (TICKET-4587).

jordan-support: I'll ask customer if they can confirm they're a business (company name & VAT ID proof) and then create the credit note. Draft message to customer: "We're sorry — we charged UK VAT by mistake due to a mismatch between your card metadata and billing details. We'll void that invoice and issue a corrected invoice showing reverse-charge (no VAT) once we confirm your VAT ID. You will receive a credit and the new invoice within 48 hours." 

liz-billing: When you create the credit note, use reason="tax_adjustment_country_mismatch" and link original invoice id. For accounting: post both the credit and the corrected invoice so totals reconcile.

tax-bot: Quick fix mitigation for now: set tax-service fallback priority to: 1) validated_vat_id_country, 2) billing_country, 3) shipping_country, 4) payment_instrument_country. I'll push a patch to staging.

ops-sre: Logged a post-deploy check to scan invoices in the last 7 days where vat_country != billing_country and vat_amount > 0 for EU customers. Query saved as monitoring/search-TAX-COUNTRY-MISMATCH.

jordan-support: Customer updated and provided VAT registration screenshot, confirmed business. I'm issuing the credit now and will follow up with the reissue. @liz-billing let me know if you want to handle the actual invoice reissue or want me to create a support draft. :thumbsup:

liz-billing: I'll take the reissue. Please attach the validation screenshot to the ticket. Mark, we'll reconcile the credit against revenue in next close.

mark-finance: Got it. Also let's add a note to our merchant docs: "If your card issuer/reporting country differs from your billing country, please provide VAT ID at purchase to avoid automatic tax fallback."

jordan-support: Closing loop with the customer once credit + reissue done. Will update thread.
